title: FACET Generation Manifest
description: Committed provenance for generated documentation (FACET §8.6), naming input resources and digests so changes can invalidate an artifact. Resource fields use in-toto ResourceDescriptor vocabulary, so a deployment that later needs signed provenance can map onto SLSA without redesigning the format.

schema_version.description: FACET schema family this manifest was written under.

artifacts.description: One entry per generated artifact, sorted by subject path so the diff stays reviewable.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file's contents. Content hashing is deliberate: git does not preserve modification times, so a timestamp comparison would mark every artifact stale after a fresh clone.

path.description: Repository-relative path to the generated file.

feature.description: Feature id the artifact was generated from.

slots.description: Knowledge slots the artifact consumed. Recording these allows per-slot staleness rather than invalidating a whole article when one unrelated slot's sources move.

generator.description: The non-hermetic part of the build. An LLM is not a deterministic compiler, so the model and prompt version are inputs: changing either invalidates the artifact exactly as a new compiler would.

generated_at.description: ISO 8601 date of generation (YYYY-MM-DD). Narration only — never used as a comparison key.

inputs.description: Everything that fed the artifact: the feature record, plus every source file anchoring that feature at generation time. The resolved set is recorded in full, because FACET resolves anchors by scanning source — an anchor added later is a real change even when every recorded digest still matches.

role.description: Input role: record is the feature record; anchor is implementing source; source-artifact is the source-language article; glossary is consulted terminology. A changed glossary invalidates artifacts that used it.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag for this artifact. A translation depends on the source-language article and record: a record change invalidates the source article, and its regeneration invalidates the translation. Records remain in their canonical language: two normative statements of one behaviour have no tie-break when they diverge.
